questions.prompt: In the final 20 days, a campaign gets a $2,000 check. What must it do?
questions.why: Contributions of $1,000 or more received in the last 20 days must be reported within 48 hours on Form 6.

questions.prompt: HMP (a super PAC) has spent $1.7M in NY's 17th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
NO GOING BACK PAC INC. (a super PAC) has spent $6.6M in NY's 3rd District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: In the final 60 days, who pays less for the same TV spot?
questions.why: Stations must sell candidates airtime at the lowest unit charge. Outside groups pay market rates, which climb near Election Day.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $838K in NV's 1st District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is offense.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
In OR's 4th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $564K. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $726K.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $2.5M in MI's 8th District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is offense.

questions.prompt: Can a super PAC give $10,000 directly to a House candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Super PACs can raise unlimited money but can't give to candidates or coordinate with them. They can only spend independently.
